topic: Primary Memory (RAM, ROM, Cache, Registers) - Computer Knowledge
description: Primary memory is the main memory of a computer that is directly accessed by the CPU. It temporarily or permanently stores data and instructions essential for immediate processing.

sections.title: Introduction to Primary Memory
sections.description: The fundamental characteristics of memory used directly by the processor to execute current tasks.

key_concepts.explanation: A type of memory where stored data is completely lost when the power supply is turned off. RAM is the primary example.
A type of memory that retains its stored data even when the power is switched off. ROM is the primary example.

important_facts.fact: Primary memory is also commonly referred to as Main Memory, Internal Memory, or Semiconductor Memory.

sections.title: Random Access Memory (RAM)
sections.description: The working memory of the computer where active programs and current data are stored for quick access.

key_concepts.explanation: Retains data as long as power is supplied without needing to be refreshed. It is extremely fast, expensive, and primarily used to build Cache memory.
Must be continually refreshed thousands of times per second to retain data. It is slower and cheaper than SRAM, and is used as the standard Main Memory in computers.

important_facts.fact: RAM is a 'Read-Write' memory, meaning the CPU can both read data from it and write data to it rapidly, though it remains highly volatile.

sections.title: Read Only Memory (ROM)
sections.description: Non-volatile memory containing crucial, permanent instructions required to start and operate the computer hardware.

key_concepts.explanation: A blank ROM chip that can be programmed only once by a user using a special device. Once written, the data cannot be erased or changed.
Data on this chip can be erased by exposing it to strong Ultraviolet (UV) light for a specific duration, allowing it to be reprogrammed.
Data can be easily erased and rewritten using electrical signals without removing the chip from the computer. Modern Flash Memory (like USB drives) is based on EEPROM technology.

key_associations.extra_info: The very first program executed when a computer is turned on, permanently stored on a ROM chip located on the motherboard.
The process of starting the computer and loading the Operating System into RAM, initiated by the instructions stored in the ROM.

sections.title: Cache Memory
sections.description: An ultra-fast memory unit acting as a buffer between the CPU and main memory to accelerate data retrieval.

key_concepts.explanation: The smallest and absolute fastest cache memory, embedded directly into the processor (CPU) chip itself.
Slightly larger and relatively slower than L1 cache, but still significantly faster than standard RAM. They feed data to the L1 cache.

important_facts.fact: The primary purpose of Cache memory is to store the most frequently used instructions and data, reducing the time the CPU wastes waiting for slower RAM.

sections.title: Registers
sections.description: The smallest, fastest, and most immediate data holding locations situated entirely within the CPU.

key_concepts.explanation: Holds the exact memory address (location) of the data or instruction that needs to be read from or written to the main memory.
A crucial register that keeps track of the sequence by holding the memory address of the very next instruction to be executed by the CPU.
A general-purpose register used by the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) to temporarily hold intermediate mathematical and logical results.

important_facts.fact: The strict hierarchy of data access speed in a computer system is: CPU Registers > Cache Memory > Main Memory (RAM) > Secondary Storage (HDD/SSD).
Registers offer the highest speed possible because they are physically integrated directly into the CPU circuitry.
